findings.message: plugins_dismissed does not strip a trailing carriage return, so a CRLF config.yaml (one saved by a Windows editor) leaves each value as `review\r`. The gsub removes only brackets, commas and quotes, and xargs does not treat \r as a separator, so `plugin_dismissed review` never matches. The hook's own section_val in hooks/session-start removes trailing whitespace, \r included, with `sed 's/[[:space:]]+$//'`, so the two readers of the same file disagree. Fix: in the plugins_dismissed awk, run `sub(/\r$/, "")` on every line before matching, or add \r to the gsub class. Add CRLF rows to the block-list table, inline and block, for both the honoured check and the fold check.
findings.scenario:
config.yaml with CRLF line endings containing `plugins:
  dismissed: [review]
`. `specclaw-suggest .specclaw review` still prints the review tip, and the session-start hook still lists the plugin, even though the user dismissed it. For a CRLF block list (`  dismissed:
    - sync
`), the hook with `github.sync: true` still prints the specclaw-sync notice.

findings.message: plugins_dismissed returns an empty list both when nothing is dismissed and when config.yaml could not be read (awk stderr goes to /dev/null). plugin_dismissed then reports 'not dismissed', so an unreadable config shows tips the user turned off. The only effect is an unwanted tip, so this stays minor. Consider having plugin_dismissed return a distinct status when the read fails, and treat that status as dismissed (no tip).

The --dismiss rewrite replaces the whole `  dismissed:` line, so any trailing comment on it is lost. That includes the template's own `# any of: review, fleet, sync, bf, extras` hint, which disappears after the first dismissal. Keep the comment when rewriting the line.
